data.name: Cecilia
data.gender_notes: Cecilia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Latin ‘caecus,’ meaning ‘blind,’ this name was given to a Christian martyr who reportedly remained devoted to her faith despite being blinded by her husband. The name Cecilia is rich in symbolism, representing the commitment and steadfastness of the faithful. The name Cecilia carries the meaning “Blind to worldly things” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cecilia usually hope their child will grow to embody blind to worldly things and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: צְלִי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: המשמעות המקורית של צליה נלקחה מהשם האכדי צל, שפירושו "שחור" או "צור". השם צליה נמצא בתנ"ך, והיא הייתה נשיאה של קהילה נוצרית ראשונה ברומא, שנספתה על ידי קיסר קלאודיוס. כיום, השם צליה נחשב לשם נשים נפוץ בעולם הנוצרי, ומייצגת את ערכי האמונה, חסד, וצדק.

in_greek.name: Κηκίλια
in_greek.long_meaning: השם Κηκίλια הוא שם אשה שנמצא בפטריארכה, והוא נגזר מהשם הלטיני Cecilia, שפירושו "השחורה" או "הסגולה". השם Κηκίλια היה נפוץ בקהילות הנוצריות ברומא, והוא מייצגת את ערכי האמונה, חסד, וצדק. בתנ"ך, השם Κηκίλια נמצא בפטריארכה, והוא הוקדש לאחת מהאשות הראשונות של הכנסייה הנוצרית.

in_latin.name: Cecilia
in_latin.long_meaning: Cecilia est nomen femineum quod originem trahit a nomine Caeli, quod est nomen Dei, et significat "tenebricosa" vel "purpurata." In Evangelio, nomen Cecilia invenitur, et est dedicata una ex primis uxoribus Ecclesiae Christianae. Caeli nomen est nomen Dei, et significat "sublimis" vel "celeritas." In Ecclesia Christiana, nomen Cecilia est nomen femineum populare, et repraesentat virtutes fidei, caritatis, et iustitiae.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Cecilia is derived from the Latin name Caeli, which means "heavenly" or "celestial." It is believed to have originated from the Etruscan word "kael," meaning "blind." In the Bible, Cecilia is mentioned as one of the first wives of the church. The name Cecilia has been a popular name for girls in the Christian tradition, symbolizing the values of faith, charity, and justice.

data.cultural_impact: Cecilia is a name of deep cultural significance, with its origins rooted in the history of the Christian faith. It is a name that has been passed down through generations, honoring the memory of a brave and dedicated martyr who sacrificed everything for her beliefs. The reputation of this early saint, who chose to remain devoted to God despite the hardships and opposition she faced, has made the name Cecilia enduringly popular among Christians.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the name Cecilia represents strength, perseverance, and unwavering commitment to one's beliefs. The story of this early martyr, who remained devoted to God despite being blinded by her husband, inspires us to remember the importance of staying true to our faith, even in the face of adversity and challenges. This name is a reminder of the power of the human spirit, and the inner strength that allows us to overcome even the most daunting obstacles. Furthermore, the name Cecilia can be seen as a symbol of spiritual blindness, reminding us of the importance of keeping our focus on the invisible realm of the divine, rather than the material world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cecilia, derived from the Latin name Caecilius, signifies 'blind' or 'hidden.' In Christianity, Saint Cecilia is revered as a patroness of music and marriage, symbolizing the hidden depths of faith and the transformative power of music that can illuminate the soul.

biblical_reference.note: Cecilia is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as one of the first wives of the church.

historical_references.reference: Cecilia was a Roman noblewoman and virgin who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Alexander Severus, around 230 AD. According to legend, she was visited by an angel who revealed her impending marriage would be to a pagan, Valerian. Cecilia refused, vowing to remain a virgin. She eventually converted her husband and her brother to Christianity and was ultimately beheaded for her faith.

The story of St. Cecilia gained popularity during the Middle Ages, with the construction of the Basilica of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere, Rome, around 800 AD. The basilica is still a popular pilgrimage site for Christians today and is believed to house Cecilia's remains.

modern_usage.modern_context: Cecilia is a name of Latin origin, and it has been deeply rooted in Christian tradition as the name of a saint and martyr. Although this historical background may not be the first association that comes to mind for modern audiences, Cecilia's name has found a contemporary relevance in several contexts. In the realm of music and arts, Cecilia is often used to evoke a feeling of elegance, creativity, and inspiration. Her name is particularly popular among musicians and artists who wish to convey a sense of sophistication and refinement. Platforms like Instagram and Pinterest are filled with accounts and boards dedicated to the name Cecilia, showcasing beautiful artwork, music compositions, and creative projects inspired by the name. TikTok has also seen a surge in usage of the name Cecilia, with users creating videos based on the name's historical significance or simply because they find it beautiful and unique. Overall, Cecilia's name continues to be a source of inspiration and creativity in various modern contexts.
